name: NestJS
description: A TypeScript NestJS API with feature modules, guards and an @nestjs/swagger contract export.

specSections.title: API Contract & Error Codes
specSections.guidance: List every endpoint under /api with its method, route, operation ID (the @ApiOperation operationId, which becomes the client method name), request and response DTO classes, the guards (AuthGuard, PermissionsGuard with @RequirePermission) and ownership rule, and the status codes it returns. Give the error table: each UPPER_SNAKE errorCode, its HTTP status and when it applies; errors are application/problem+json with errorCode from the global ProblemDetailsFilter, and ValidationPipe errors are 400 with an errors map. Name the auth scheme (session cookie for same-origin, JWT for cross-origin) and the Terminus health endpoints /api/health/live and /api/health/ready.

order.reason: Change the contract (backend/openapi/api.json) before regenerating the frontend client from it.

generatedFiles.ciCheck: cd {be} && npm run openapi:export && git diff --exit-code openapi/api.json

requiredEnv.description: The database URI (postgresql://…), validated by the ConfigModule schema and used by the data provider; sslmode=require for managed hosts.
Comma-separated frontend origins passed to app.enableCors (cross-origin model only).

checklist.item: Feature modules with thin controllers and orchestrating services; domain rules are pure and unit-tested by FR.
Controllers return DTOs (documented with @ApiOkResponse/@ApiResponse), never ORM entities.
A global ValidationPipe (whitelist, forbidNonWhitelisted, transform) and ProblemDetailsFilter return application/problem+json with the spec's errorCodes.
AuthGuard and PermissionsGuard plus ownership checks protect every protected route; Throttler on auth routes; CORS only for cross-origin with explicit origins.
Config is validated at boot (ConfigModule validate) and no secrets are committed.
Health uses Terminus with /api/health/live (no checks) and /api/health/ready (DB ping).
e2e tests cover success, 400, 401, 403, 404, each errorCode and 409 per FR, against a Testcontainers Postgres.
Operation IDs are stable, the export runs without a DB, openapi/api.json is fresh (CI check), and the gate passes.

gate: cd {be} && npm ci && npm run lint && npm run build && npm test && npm run test:e2e
cd {be} && npm run openapi:export && git diff --exit-code openapi/api.json
